0.2.0.lead: AI programs can now do everything you can do in nexlore, and you decide per tool what they may do on their own. Spaces can be renamed, people appear under a name of their own choosing, and nexlore tells you when a newer version is out.

sections.title: AI from outside can do everything, with rights per tool
sections.where: Account menu, My account, AI, a key, Rights per tool
sections.body: Over MCP an AI program now makes spaces, folders and notes, renames and moves them with their links, and works with versions, the trash, tags, comments and attachments. Under each key you set every tool to Allow, Ask or Deny. New keys read freely, ask before they make or change something, and do not even see the tools that delete, share or change members. The operator can block tools for everybody.

sections.title: Approvals
sections.where: Account menu, Approvals, and New since your last visit
sections.body: A tool set to Ask waits for you. The request shows with exactly what the program sent; Approve and run does exactly that, Decline does nothing, and after 24 hours it runs out. With a tick the tool runs without asking from then on.

sections.title: Connectors
sections.where: My account, AI, How to connect a program
sections.body: Programs that sign in themselves need only the address of nexlore with /api/mcp after it. You sign in, choose the level and the spaces, and agree; the program then stands in the list like a key. For AI apps that run in the cloud, nexlore must be reachable from the internet; a program on your own computer reaches it at home.

sections.title: Rename a space
sections.where: Sidebar, right click on a space, Rename
sections.body: For the managers of a space. Links that name the space in front, like [[Space/Note]], follow in every space, and so do favorites, public pages, drafts and the home space of every account. Links without the name stay as they are.

sections.title: A display name for every account
sections.where: Account menu, My account, Profile, Display name
sections.body: Each account chooses how others see it, for example with first and last name. In member lists and in the @ suggestions the sign-in name stays beside it, because that is what goes into the text after @.

sections.title: About nexlore, with an update check
sections.body: The version, the licence, the source code and the releases. Once a day nexlore asks GitHub whether a newer version is out; only that question goes out. The operator can switch it off there and check by hand.

small: The settings moved into the account menu, as in Nexview; the header keeps the places you work in.
This window comes once per version with news, for every account.

0.3.0.lead: nexlore now tells you when something needs you: by webhook, and by mail when the operator set up a mail server. You choose for each occasion whether you hear about it.

sections.title: Notifications
sections.body: Give a webhook address, a notification inbox for example, and switch mail on if your operator set up a mail server. Then choose what you hear about: somebody names you with @ or answers in your thread, an invitation or an approval for an AI program waits, and once a day at a time of your choosing, what is due today or overdue. Send a test shows at once whether it arrives. A notification names the note and who did something, never what a note or a comment says.

sections.title: Server troubles reach the operator
sections.where: Account menu, My account, Notifications, Server troubles
sections.body: Operators hear when a scheduled backup failed, when a newer version of nexlore is out and when the disk where nexlore keeps its data runs full. Each of these comes once, not every minute.

small: Moving a note to the trash right after opening the dialog takes the files only this note uses along again; before, they could stay behind.

0.4.0.lead: nexlore now works with programs such as n8n and nexdeck. An API token reads your notes, tasks and the numbers for a dashboard, and if you want it also writes: makes, changes, appends, ticks off. It can never delete, move or share.

sections.title: API tokens for programs
sections.where: Account menu, My account, Connections, API tokens
sections.body: Make a token of its own for each program: read or write, for all your spaces or only some, and if you like running out after 30 days, 90 days or a year. The token is shown once, with the header line for n8n and a command to try it. What a program writes becomes a version with the source “Program (API)”; when the note changed meanwhile or somebody is editing it, the text goes into a conflict copy.

sections.title: The operator holds the latch
sections.where: Settings, Server, AI, API and plugins, API tokens
sections.body: API tokens are off by default. The operator switches them on, sees every token with its account, level and last use, never the token itself, and can block one for good. Switched off, every token answers 401 until they are switched on again.

small: A week before one of your API tokens runs out, it stands out in yellow in the list, and nexlore tells you (My account, Notifications, can be switched off).
The part of the server settings is now called “AI, API and plugins”.

0.4.1.lead: A link to a heading now takes you right there, and a few things that did not work as they should are repaired.

sections.title: Links jump to the heading
sections.where: Any note with a link like [[Note#Heading]]
sections.body: A click on a link to a heading no longer opens the note at the very top but right at that heading, while reading as in the editor, and on the title of an embedded part too. Upper or lower case does not matter. If you leave out the note's name, as in [[#Heading]], you jump within the same note.

small: A link like [[#Heading]] no longer shows pale as a missing note, and cleaning up no longer lists it among the links to nothing.
The detail of the log can be turned up for an hour again; before, the choice quietly fell back.
Callouts of the kinds question, help and faq are yellow in the editor as when reading, no longer violet.
A few texts still named the old way “My account, AI”; they now lead through Connections.
